_about: The owed shores' data (ruling 234, the design director's notes of 22:05Z and 22:10Z of 20 November 2026 on the second rules builder's table, pacific-six/allin-1754/b644/shores-table.md, with the historian's rows: historian/south-landings-record-1941-42.md, sections 7 and 8). A seats file, kept by hand and laid last by src/campaign/far-rows.ts while the far side's switch is on. Weights use the game's own count, 15,000 men to a division. The 'rows' block is the far side's own: amendments, by country and name, to rows that far-world.json and far-seats-pacific.json lay. Those two files are written by their tools from the planner's and the historian's files and never by hand; when their sources take these figures the amendments go.
_weights: Rabaul: the South Seas Detachment 0.33 (about 5,000 men), Lark Force 0.09 (about 1,400). Wake: the garrison capped at its record 0.035 (about 520 fighting men), the landing force at the second try's 0.10 (about 1,500). Midway starts at 0.06 (about 900 Marines in December 1941) and fills by drafts to a cap of 0.2 (about 3,000 by June 1942). Samoa: the 7th Defense Battalion 0.05; the 2nd Marine Brigade (about 4,800 men, 0.32) comes as its own row in January 1942. Every outpost row now carries a cap.
_regiments: The 38th Division comes as three regimental rows where no book dates Japan's rows (stops 3 to 5): the 228th (the Ito Detachment), 0.3, for Ambon and then Timor; the 229th with the division's headquarters and its general, 0.3, for Palembang; the 230th (the Shoji Detachment), 0.3 with its tank company and the airfield group (0.27 until the Indies' record of 21 November 2026), for Bandoeng's Java Sea coast, Eretan Wetan's ground on this chart: the record's aim was Kalidjati's airfield, which this chart does not set apart from Bandoeng's ground. All three stand at Canton from month 2 as the division did, are held for the plan as it was (rider b423), and take Hong Kong first. At stops 1 and 2 the book keeps the division's row and its own Shoji rows as they were: the division's row is marked for those stops. The fronts and their follow-ons are in far-pacific-war.json.
_works: 'works' is [province, months]: the works the row has where the record's landing came, in place of the rule that every corps left alone digs in whole (game.ts digIn). 0 none, 1 begun. No works at Merak and Bantam Bay (the KNIL 1st Division, Batavia), at Kragan (the 2nd, Semarang), at Eretan (the mobilisation row, Bandoeng) or on Sumatra's beaches (Medan). Field positions and no finished works at Rabaul (Lark Force); light field defences at most at Palembang. Gull Force at Laha and the Great East garrisons at Paso are dug in by the rule and carry no flag; so are Blackforce and the Texans. Wake's, Midway's and Samoa's rows are fortress troops, which the rule does not read; the coast batteries at Tandjong Priok and Soerabaja are the provinces' own works and stand.
_will: 'will' is where the row's morale settles when nothing is happening to it, in place of morale.json's level of 0.5 (the historian's orders, marked M; the figures are the second rules builder's, set within them as the director ruled at 22:10Z). A band of the game's words for morale is 0.2 wide. The KNIL's rows sit one band below the common level, 0.3: well below the Australians. The Sumatra garrisons, where Atjeh rose, and Lark Force, told it would have no relief and no way out, sit a band and a half below, 0.2. Wake's Marines, Gull Force, Blackforce and the Texans are steady and carry no flag.
_indies: The Indies' owed shores at the record's weights (ruling 234, the design director's notes of 23:50Z of 20 November and 04:47Z of 21 November 2026 on the parts table, beside the historian's palembang-tarakan-record.md and south-landings-record-1941-42.md; if the historian's check of each owner's scale moves a figure, its line is laid again): the Sakaguchi Detachment 0.33 (about 5,000 men; the 56th Division later adds the rest, 0.67); Tarakan's garrison, the KNIL's 7th Battalion with its gunners, 0.09, its works not met where the night landing came, its will the KNIL's; Palembang's garrison 0.15 over three places; Ambon's KNIL about 2,600 men, 0.17, and Gull Force about 1,100, 0.07; Koepang's Sparrow Force about 1,400 with the KNIL's Timor garrison of about 600, 0.13 in the one row. The Indies' record of 21 November 2026 (the historian's indies-landings-1941-42.md, accepted as data, middles, by the director at 15:16Z and ordered laid at 15:27Z: a fact is never held back, nor laid, to move a reading). Ambon: the Great East row is the Molukken Brigade alone, about 2,800 men, 0.19 (its quality in far-pacific-war.json), and the row is split by place: the Celebes' garrisons are first-day rows of their own under 'world' here, Menado's about 1,500 men, 0.1, and Kendari's about 400, 0.03 (the historian's japan-second-ring-b599.md), neither with works where the landings came; Makassar's is the KNIL's South Celebes command, about 1,000 men, 0.07, at 0.7 (the historian's japan-taken-towns-1942.md of 21 November 2026, section 1: native regulars with militia and Landstorm, who had planned not to fight for the town; no works met; Menado's are the Menadonese, 0.85, by the same table); Timor's is in Sparrow Force's row. The naval landing forces' Kure row is the 1st Kure force alone, about 800 men, 0.05: the 2nd went with the Sakaguchi Detachment to Tarakan and is in its 0.33 (the row keeps its name, which a line here cannot change). Borneo: the Kawaguchi Detachment 0.325 (the 124th Regiment with the 35th Brigade's staff, about 4,900 men), its follow-ons in far-pacific-war.json; Kuching's defence 0.1, the 2/15th Punjab about 1,000 with the Sarawak Rangers and volunteers, in the one row. Java: the 2nd Division's row stands at 1.0 when it sails, a one-division row's ceiling, so the record's 1.1 with the army's troops is not laid; the Sakaguchi Detachment keeps its 0.33, the record's 0.3 at Kragan coming after its fights at Tarakan and Balikpapan. The 2nd Division's 1.1 at Merak (the director's 16:08Z of 21 November 2026): the division's row is laid at its cap, 1.0, and the 0.1 above it is the 16th Army's troops landing with it, a row of their own in the form of Hong Kong's guns: where no book dates Japan's rows (stops 3 to 5) they gather at Cam Ranh a month after the war with Britain begins, stand beside the division from the month after (far-pacific-war.json, history.stations, 'beside'), and go with it to Batavia: the plan's follow-on names them. The cap stays and the record's middle is kept. Singkawang (the same note: anything in the historian's file with a place on the chart is laid): the KNIL's West Borneo detachment at the Singkawang II airfield, about 0.05, a first-day row under 'world', no works where the column from Kuching came. Both rows that land beside another, Palembang's paratroops and the 16th Army's troops, come at every stop of the dial (the director's 16:18Z: the record's rows belong at every stop where their landing is made from rows): at the book's stops each is named in its landing's dated attack and sails in its lead's lift as the tank regiments do, the paratroops beside the book's own row for the 229th; the record's met figures there are untouched, so the book's fights are as they were and the rows stand ashore after.
_kwangsi: The Southern Kwangtung garrison, Pakhoi's row on the shore of Qinzhou Bay: 0.15 with a cap and no works (the historian's kwangsi-landing-and-garrison-totals.md, section 1, accepted as data by the design director at 23:21Z of 20 November 2026). The record's landing of 15 November 1939 met a few thousand provincial troops and militia, about 0.1 to 0.2 with no works of note, who fell back; the row stood at 0.4, dug in whole by the rule, and threw the book's landing back. The town's own guard is the rule's (siege.json) and is not this file's to change.
_burma: Burma's rows at the record's weights (ruling 234, the design director's notes of 04:47Z to 05:00Z, 05:30Z and 05:35Z of 21 November 2026, beside the historian's strength-and-attacks-b573.md, china-scale-restatement.md, far-chart-airfields.md sections 5 and 6 and coast-group-armies-and-burma-elites.md section 2). Britain's: the Burma Army never fills past 0.5 (the 1st Burma Division); the 17th Indian Division comes at 0.6 and fills to 0.75 (the 48th Gurkha Brigade joined it within the month; the game fills it by its drafts); the 7th Armoured Brigade 0.35 (about 114 light tanks). China's armies, under Britain's flag in the game, stand at China's scale of about 40,000 men at a place to 1.0: the 5th 0.55, the 6th 0.45, the 66th 0.45. What the 200th, the 22nd and the 38th Divisions were worth beyond their numbers is their rows' quality in far-pacific-war.json (history.stations.raised: 0.65 for the 5th Army, 0.55 for the 66th), which a fight multiplies by the weight: it is counted there once and not in the weight as well. Japan's 15th Army is about 1.4, not 2.0. By the book (stops 1 and 2) its row stays where the book's own attacks find it, at 0.7 a division. Where no book dates Japan's rows (stops 3 to 5) it is counted from the strike: the 55th Division's 143rd Regiment (the Uno Detachment), 0.28, waits at Saigon with the strike's rows, is on the Kra the day the strike goes (a move by land of the plan's Burma front, far-pacific-war.json) and is that front's in the field against Mergui's ground, where Victoria Point lies; the army's body, 0.56 a division (1.12: the rest of the 55th and the 33rd with two regiments), forms at Raheng a month after the war with Britain begins, before the Kawkareik road to Moulmein. The plan's Burma front ends at Myitkyina, the campaign's end of May 1942, and the 56th and 18th Divisions are on its list. The 18th Division came to Rangoon in April 1942 without its 124th Regiment, the Kawaguchi Detachment: its row, at every stop, is made of the 25th Army's 18th Division alone, 0.65, and the detachment stays its own row.
_palembang: Palembang's whole force (the design director's notes of 05:30Z and 05:35Z of 21 November 2026 to ruling 234; the historian's far-chart-airfields.md, section 7, and palembang-tarakan-record.md). The 229th Regiment's 0.3 was laid without the paratroops who took the P1 airfield and the refineries ahead of it: the army's 2nd Raiding Regiment, about 460 men, 0.03: about 360 dropped on 14 February 1942 and about 100 more on the 15th (0.025, the first day's drop alone, until the Indies' record of 21 November 2026). Palembang's defence of 0.15 is that record's KNIL, about 2,000 men, 0.13, with the British anti-aircraft gunners at P1 and the refineries, 0.02, in the one row. Where no book dates Japan's rows (stops 3 to 5) it gathers at Phnom Penh a month after the war with Britain begins and goes with the 229th to Palembang: the plan's follow-on names it (far-pacific-war.json), and it sails in the regiment's lift (history.stations, 'beside'). It dropped from Johore's airfields, which the follow-on already waits for; the rules land an airborne force by itself or not at all, so it joins the 229th's fight in the same month and no seizure ahead of the landing is counted. It is airborne troops by its mark. Its quality is a line regiment's: picked men, who jumped with pistols and grenades. The part of the 229th that landed at Muntok stays in the 0.3: the chart has no Banka.
_oahu: Oahu's divisions as the record has them (the design director's notes of 06:09Z, 06:12Z and 06:21Z of 21 November 2026 to ruling 234; the historian's far-chart-town-guards-globe.md, section 5). The Hawaiian Division stands from the first day at 0.7, never past 0.8. In October 1940 (month 14) the two Hawaii National Guard regiments are called into federal service, new men and so arrivals: the 298th Infantry beside the division at Pearl Harbor (0.11, never past 0.15), and the 299th's battalions on Hawaii, Maui and Kauai (0.04, 0.035 and 0.035, never past 0.05 each, held to their islands). On 1 October 1941 (month 26) the division is split: the 25th Infantry Division is made at Honolulu from the 298th and from the division (it asks 0.55: the Guard regiment whole and two of the four Regular regiments), and the 24th Infantry Division is made at Pearl Harbor from what is left of the Hawaiian Division, whose name goes. The 25th never past 0.8; the 24th never past 0.65 on Oahu, which with the 299th's 0.15 on the outer islands is the record's division of 0.8 (the 299th was its third regiment: at 0.8 beside those rows its men would be counted twice). A row made from corps on the board ('from' in the formations list, game.ts startPhase, far side) takes its strength out of them and never more than they hold, and does not come where none of them is left: a reorganisation makes nothing from nothing, and a computer America, which is sent no dated expedition (world.ts shipsItsOwn), has its reorganisations here. The gap, recorded with its cause and not stood in for by any dated cap or row: the record has the island at about 1.0 by the end of 1940, 1.3 in September 1941 and 1.6 in December 1941 as drafted men filled the regiments through 1941; the rows' caps let the island stand at no more than 0.95 before the split (as read with no fighting, a computer America: 0.86 in October 1940, 0.94 in September 1941), and from the split the chart's own fill carries the two divisions toward their caps (1.01 in October 1941, 1.33 in December, 1.45 from March 1942), with 0.15 on the outer islands. No row for the Marines at Pearl Harbor: Midway's row fills from 0.06 to 0.2, which is the men that pool sent out.
_src: 'src' on a line names the tool-written file whose row it amends (the director, 23:18Z of 20 November 2026, 1). A line that names no row of its list stops the game at once (far-rows.ts amendRow), so a rename never drops a figure silently. A line leaves when its source's tool takes the figure.
_flag: The KNIL mobilisation row comes as Dutch, as the KNIL's standing rows do, and changes flag with them on its cause, the fall of the Netherlands, never on a date (game.ts keptLevy, pacific.ts keptForces). Its month stays: the Indies began to enlarge its militia after May 1940.
_guards: The small islands' guards after capture (the design director, 00:46Z of 21 November 2026, on the historian's north-china-oob-and-island-guards.md, section 2): once taken, a small island far from a front was held by a navy guard unit or a detachment of a base force, a few hundred men, and the army came only when a front drew near. Each is a row at the record's weight, held and staying, dated the month after the record's capture and posted to its place: Guam 0.03 (the 54th Guard Unit; the South Seas Detachment left for Rabaul in January 1942), Kendari 0.04 (the navy's air base and its guard), Menado 0.02, Biak 0.02, Guadalcanal 0.02 (the guard of the airfield begun in July 1942; the construction units' 2,500 workers were not fighters). Where the place is not Japan's on the date the row comes ashore at Japan's nearest held port and the staff posts it (rider b642 part 2, game.ts ashoreFor). Morotai stays empty, as the record had it. Biak's guard stands until a row for the army's 222nd Regiment (December 1943) is laid; no file has one yet. The war each row waits for is the one that takes its island: the Dutch islands and the Solomons are taken in Japan's war with Britain, as the planner's rows for them have it. From the director's 16:44Z of 21 November 2026 the five are dated at the book's stops alone ('stops' [1, 2]); at stops 3 to 5 they fold into the rear garrison by cause ('open'.rear below, '_rear'), each at its figure here.
_21st: The 21st Division at the book's stops (the design director's 19:40Z (g) and 19:56Z of 21 November 2026; the historian's japan-taken-towns-1942.md, sections 9 and 10). The record: the division passed to the Southern Army in November 1941, left the Tientsin-Pukow railway in month 27 and landed in Tonkin in month 30, less the detachment it sent to Bataan; its stretch at Hsuchow was taken by the 17th Division, which the chart has from the first day inside the 13th Army's row at Pengpu, so no new division is laid: from month 27 Hsuchow stands at about 0.5 and Pengpu at about 0.4 (the historian's shift, L), the men of the two old rows and no more (1.8 before, 0.5 + 0.4 + 0.65 + 0.25 after). In September 1943 the 17th sailed for Rabaul (first echelon ashore month 50, about 0.6 to 0.7) and the 65th Division, a security division formed that year, held Hsuchow to 1945 (about 0.55). Stops 1 and 2 only: at stops 3 to 5 nothing moves by a date, the division stays at Hsuchow and the old month-30 cut for Bataan stands (marked stops 3 to 5 here).
_rear: The rear garrison of a taken port (the design director's rulings of 16:36Z, 16:44Z and 16:46Z of 21 November 2026, on the trace pacific-r2/membership/READ-STOOD-12.md and the historian's japan-taken-towns-1942.md, sections 3 to 6). In 12 wars a landing force alone in the port it had taken was kept there by the last-guard rule for 400 province-months, Rabaul's in every war: the rule worked and the record's rear was missing. No taken port was left empty: a navy base force in the navy's ground, garrison and line-of-communication troops in the army's, took each port over within weeks and the landing force went on. 'open'.rear: at the stops in 'stops' a computer staff's taken port (or city the last guard binds) on ground taken from a country in its table's 'of' gets a row of its own the month after it is taken, while held, once for each taking, never by date alone; it holds and stays; its weight is drawn from its owner's reserve of men as it comes and none comes while the reserve cannot give it (staff.ts rearMonth). 'towns' are the record's figures at their middles, [divisions' worth, the row's name]: 0.1 at a base force's seat, the town's own figure where the historian gives one, and 'each' (0.05, a lesser port) for a port the table does not name. Guam, Kendari, Menado, Biak and Guadalcanal keep the figures and names of their dated rows ('_guards'). Each owner reads its own table and nobody another's (the director's 19:24Z: the form is by owner): Japan's first; the United States' and Britain's from historian/rear-garrisons-us-britain-1941-45.md, a base command (a base section, an island command with its defense battalion, a sub-area) at the middle of 0.05 to 0.1, 0.075, with Saipan's island command at the historian's 0.2. 'of' is whose ground the table covers: China's is in nobody's (its taken towns have rider C's garrison ask, and one ground gets one rule). Taken means taken in war from an enemy still fought; a living ally's freed port is that ally's again and gets that ally's own row, as a country's own port does when it takes it back (the director's 19:40Z: Tarawa, Britain's; Guam's island command at the historian's 0.2); ground that passed into keeping as its owner fell was not taken. Australia's is a base sub-area at about 0.1 for a port it takes or takes back (Lae, Finschhafen; Buna's base 0.05), from the same file's section 2b (the director's 19:56Z); New Zealand's brigades stood at places the chart does not have (Vella Lavella, the Treasuries, Green Island), so it has no table yet. It is one rule for everybody (the director's 19:44Z): a player's country gets the same row at the same cost, and 'says' is the line his month's report carries. At the book's stops the record's dated rows hold the ports and nothing comes from here.
_khalkhin: The two Khalkhin Gol rows hold (the design director, 19:30Z of 21 November 2026, form B, on the second rules builder's read of that day): release 1's event of eastern Poland takes every Soviet corps that is not held and stands them in turn on its six places, so with the whole world on the chart the 1st Army Group and its tanks left Tamsag Bulak for Polesie and Wilno in the war's first month. The record kept the group in Mongolia (the 17th Army from 1940, to 1945; historian/soviet-far-east-1941-45.md): its two rows hold and stay like the other sixteen rows of the Soviet Far East. The event is as it was; the Far East's real transfers west are after release.
_borneo: The Kawaguchi Detachment's split (the design director's rulings of 07:16Z and 07:40Z of 22 November 2026, on the historian's second-division-and-british-borneo-1941-42.md, section 4; it replaces one row, one corps). The record gives no battalion numbers, so the shares are the historian's working (two battalions to Kuching, one left at Miri; a battalion about 0.07, marked unsure), taken as proportions of the row's ruled size: the row stands at 0.325 from the earlier reading of the same paper (sections 2 and 3), the shares sum to 0.3, and each is 0.325 / 0.3 of its figure. The book's stops only. In December 1941 the whole detachment makes Miri, Brunei and Kuching (far-pacific-war.json, the dated attacks), Kuching's fight at the record's 0.2. In January 1942 it is four rows: the western force 0.14 at Kuching (the record's 0.13, overland and by sea as one row at the chart's grain), which takes the detachment off the board, and three cut from it by that row: the Kuching guard 0.055 (0.05), which stays; the North Borneo battalion 0.075 (0.07) at Miri, for Jesselton and Sandakan; the Miri and Seria party 0.0325 (0.03), which stays. They sum to 0.3025: the record's loss off Kuching on 23 December is the rest, and the game's own fight for Kuching takes its own. At stops 3 to 5 the detachment is one row and its staff's, as it was. Where its men came from (the design director, 11:42Z of 22 November 2026, a note only): the detachment was formed from the 18th Division's 124th Infantry Regiment. A dated row strikes off the corps it names and comes at its written worth, so nothing is drawn from the division for it: the detachment's 0.325 and the 25th Army's 18th Division at 0.65 stand as written, and the 0.025 they leave of the division ends with its Canton row (china-setup.json; the 09:00Z ruling).
_palau: G (a stand-in, to be read by the historian before the gate; a G never stays past it unread): the Kure 1st and 2nd landing forces (for Legaspi and Davao) are staged at Palau, not Yap, laid by the design director, 14:28Z, 25 November 2026, (c), from the historian's lean of 14:26Z (island-room-answers-1125.md, section 1: 'Staged at Palau, not Yap', memory). The row's 'at' below; far-world.json is the planner's (tools/make-far-world.mjs from pacific-planner/opening-armies.json, which still says Yap) and is not edited by hand. Palau's room is 2 divisions' worth of men since the island's room is counted in men.
_luzon1944: The Tsuda Detachment (the design director's ruling of 07:33Z of 22 November 2026, on the historian's luzon-leyte-1944-45-2nd-tank-26th.md): the part of the 26th Division left on Luzon when the division sailed for Ormoc in November 1944, the 11th Independent Infantry less a battalion, about 0.125 (the middle of 0.1 to 0.15, marked unsure). The book's stops only; its stations and the division's are far-pacific-war.json's late rows. At stops 3 to 5 the 26th Division is one row at its present size.
